messages:
alex: Heads up — seeing a new p99 tail spike on the dedicated-gpu pool for runtime v1.24.0 when concurrency ~1.2k. p50/p95/p99 from the trace sampler  — 9ms / 112ms / 620ms. Raising here before we escalate to oncall.

maria: Do we have kernel fallback logs? Could be attention kernel mismatch at longer seq len.

alex: Quick profiler dump from the host (snip):
```
2026-03-18 10:12:04 host-17 runtime-profiler
active_requests: 1248
kernel_selection: attention_v2 (38%) -> attention_generic fallback (62%)
microbatch_size: 16
kv_cache_miss_rate: 14.3%
evictions_per_min: 168
median_kv_lookup_ms: 0.8ms
kv_rebuild_sync_ms (when miss): 42ms
request_latency_ms (sample): p50=9, p95=112, p99=620
```

jp: That kv_rebuild_sync on miss looks huge — if a lot of requests miss and do a sync rebuild we blow the tail. Are evictions correlated with traffic spikes?

li: I checked shard-level metrics — when concurrency > ~900 we see eviction churn on top hot partitions. Cache occupancy oscillates 0.4 -> 0.18 -> rebuild -> 0.46 in short window. Looks like microbatching + kernel routing timing amplifies it.

maria: Two hypotheses: (1) cache pressure causes synchronous KV loads on hot requests which serializes the pipeline and increases p99, (2) kernel fallback to generic (slower) happens when sequence lengths deviate and we lose optimized kernels, compounding tail.

alex: Agreed. Short term mitigation ideas: bump per-vm cache limit by 25% for the affected pool; reduce microbatch to 8 to reduce head-of-line wait for hot keys; and pin attention_v2 for models with seq<=512 so we avoid fallback. Which is least risky?

jp: Reducing microbatch reduces throughput but should lower single-request enqueue wait — good for latency SLOs. Bumping cache size is low-risk but might just postpone churn. Pinning kernel needs model-surface validation.

li: I can run a quick canary: two nodes with config changes — nodeA: microbatch=8, nodeB: cache_size *1.25. Compare p95/p99 over 5m window.

amybot (infra-bot): Canary job created: canary/kv-tail-1759329999 — nodes: nodeA (mb=8), nodeB (cache+25%). Results ETA ~10m.

maria: Also add logging for "kv_rebuild_sync_ms" to trace and add a histogram for time spent rebuilding per-request (so we can separate rebuild cost vs kernel cost).

alex: Quick note on routing: if kernel selector flips to generic we should fallback to scaled CPU backoff path OR route to lower-latency variant. Could we try forcing attention_v2 for the canary to see effect?

li: I'll include a nodeC with kernel_force=attention_v2 (for pinned models) — nodeC will be isolated to non-critical traffic.

jp: One more: try a transient eviction-throttle flag (prevent evictions for 30s at peak) to see if preventing churn reduces p99. If it helps, we can tune real eviction heuristics.

alex: Good. For tracking:
- li: run canary nodes A/B/C and collect p50/p95/p99 + kv_rebuild histograms (owner)
- maria: add rebuild histogram and dashboard panel (owner)
- jp: test transient eviction-throttle on dev cluster and share script (owner)

deploy-bot: canary/kv-tail-1759329999 deployed: nodeA,nodeB,nodeC (staged).

li: First 6m of canary: nodeA(mb=8) p95=78ms p99=260ms; nodeB(cache+25%) p95=98ms p99=420ms; nodeC(kernel_force) p95=64ms p99=190ms. Rebuild histograms show nodeC had 60% fewer sync rebuilds.

maria: Interesting — forcing the kernel and reducing kernel fallback seems to have the biggest p99 benefit. That suggests fallback + rebuild compounding the tail.

jp: From dev run of eviction-throttle: tail reduced by ~30% but throughput dropped 8% (backpressure build-up). So throttling helps latency but at throughput cost — expected tradeoff.

alex: Proposed next steps before rolling: (1) increase per-shard cache floor by 20% in dedicated pool, (2) revert microbatch to 8 for latency-tier customers, (3) adjust kernel selector to prefer attention_v2 unless sequence length > 1024, and (4) rework eviction heuristic to avoid rapid oscillation (increase hysteresis).

li: I'll open infra PR for cache floor + canary rollout plan.

maria: I'll draft a short postmortem note once we have 24h of data; include perf regression tags and rollout timeline.

alex: Thanks all. If anyone sees new spikes ping here or add @oncall.

jp: sharing quick script to repro locally (dev):
```bash
# simulate hot-key churn workload
python tools/loadgen.py --concurrency 1200 --hot_ratio 0.8 --seq 512 --duration 300
```

li: adding to runbook under "kv-cache-churn".

alex: closing for now, will reopen if canary diverges. :thumbsup:
